epic.intent:
Prove that the packaged app and its headless MCP entry work across operating systems and agent hosts.

Carried over from the retired markdown board (`board/in-progress/014-cross-host-release.md`, milestone 6). Its first two parts are done: 014.1 packaged the MCP entry with the app, and 014.2 added the skill install wrapper. This epic holds the two open parts, 014.3 and 014.4.

successCriteria.text: Packaged Windows (NSIS and portable) and macOS (arm64 and x64) builds each start the desktop app and the MCP entry against one shared database.
A second MCP host completes a sprint through MCP using the same saved plan, without changing any stored ticket requirements.

epic.title: Cross-host validation and release

bundle.rationale: The second-host run uses the packaged MCP entry, so it waits until the packaged builds are verified. One sprint, because both parts are verification work with no code expected.

exitCriteria.text: Evidence (logs or screenshots) from Windows and from macOS arm64 and x64 shows desktop and MCP sharing one database.
A second host completed a sprint on the same plan, with its run events attached.

sprints.goal: The packaged app and MCP entry are verified on Windows and macOS and from a second agent host.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The packaged Windows NSIS and portable builds start the desktop app and the MCP entry with a shared database.
The packaged macOS arm64 and x64 builds do the same.
The installed-app `npm run smoke:mcp` passes on each platform, with output attached.

tickets.body:
Formerly board ticket 014.3. This needs real Windows and macOS machines or CI runners; a Linux container can't verify it.

For each packaged build (Windows NSIS installer, Windows portable, macOS `.dmg` arm64 and x64):
1. Install, launch the desktop app, and track and initialize a scratch repository.
2. Start the MCP entry with the app executable and `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` (see `docs/runbooks/mcp-setup.md`) against the same repository.
3. Create an epic over MCP and confirm the desktop shows it. Then save a plan in the desktop and confirm `get_plan` over MCP returns it.

The installed-app smoke test (`MCP_SMOKE_COMMAND=... MCP_SMOKE_SERVER=... npm run smoke:mcp`) covers the MCP half on each machine.

reasoning.rationale: Manual cross-platform verification with careful evidence gathering.

tickets.title: Verify the Windows and macOS packaged builds share one database between desktop and MCP

acceptanceCriteria.text: A second MCP host completes a sprint through MCP using the same saved plan.
The saved plan revision and ticket capability requirements are unchanged before and after the run.
Run events and the sprint report from the second host are attached.

tickets.body:
Formerly board ticket 014.4. Run the same planning and execution contract from a second MCP host, a different agent host from the one that planned the epic, without changing the stored ticket requirements.

Use a small saved epic in a scratch repository. Connect the second host with the packaged app's MCP entry, run one sprint as orchestrator (claim, submit, accept), and file the sprint report. A person approves the checkpoint in the desktop app.

reasoning.rationale: End-to-end interop run that has to follow the orchestrator contract exactly.

tickets.title: Complete a sprint from a second MCP host on the same plan
